why: OFFER ARITHMETIC (OA 9.2, Book Value): 6.1% x $3,100,000 members' equity (most recent year-end balance sheet) = $189,100. INDEPENDENT INDICATION (broker, 2026-10-05): enterprise value $14,500,000, equity value approx. $9,800,000 (implied net debt/other $4,700,000); 18% x $9,800,000 = $1,764,000; 6.1% x $9,800,000 = $597,800. GAPS: offer is 10.72% of the independent value of the 18% interest ($189,100 / $1,764,000); the offer is $1,574,900 below the 18% indication, $408,700 below even the 6.1% indication, and $368,900 below what 9.2 would yield at her pre-call 18% (18% x $3,100,000 = $558,000). Book equity $3,100,000 understates the independent equity indication by $6,700,000 (68.4%). WHY THE DILUTION IS NOT VALID ON THIS FILE (three independent defects, each sufficient): (1) DELIVERY MECHANICS - OA 6.3 requires written notice 'delivered to each Member by certified mail and email.' The 2026-08-20 call was sent by text message with a PDF; no certified mail was ever sent; the email bounced to an old address on file. All three facts confirmed by the client 2026-10-08 (texted PDF only; 'no letter'; email on file is from 2019 and dead), but so was actual receipt: she saw the text and PDF on 2026-08-20 and did not respond, assuming 'it wasn't real notice'. The library rule is strict compliance with notice mechanics, and a call that fails the specified delivery method does not trigger dilution; the fight is now purely delivery-method compliance, not lack of knowledge. Timing was NOT a defect: 2026-08-20 to 2026-09-20 is 31 days, satisfying 'at least 30 days.' (2) PURPOSE - 6.3 requires 'a bona fide Company purpose set forth in the call notice'; the notice stated only 'working capital and opportunities' (open-ended), and Bram then funded the whole $1,500,000 himself, including her $270,000, and moved to dilute and buy at book value within 5 days of the due date - a pretext pattern that must be proved with the actual use of the $1,500,000. (3) FAIR VALUE / GOOD FAITH - dilution is 'pro rata based on the fair value of the Company as determined by the Manager in good faith'; the Manager's $7,200,000 is 26.53% below the independent equity indication (($9,800,000-$7,200,000)/$9,800,000) and 50.34% below the independent enterprise value (($14,500,000-$7,200,000)/$14,500,000), and the library makes such a determination reviewable under the implied covenant where the value is far below a contemporaneous independent indication. ARITHMETIC THAT DOES NOT RECONCILE (left open, not forced): the 6.1% figure cannot be derived from any pro rata formula using the Manager's own $7,200,000. On the natural value-weighted reading - her pre-call 18% of fair value, no new cash of her own, Bram contributing all $1,500,000 - 18% x $7,200,000 / ($7,200,000 + $1,500,000) = $1,296,000/$8,700,000 = 14.90%; at the independent equity value 18% x $9,800,000 / ($9,800,000 + $1,500,000) = $1,764,000/$11,300,000 = 15.61%; at enterprise value $14,500,000 it is 16.31%; on a book-equity weighting it is 18% x $3,100,000 / ($3,100,000 + $1,500,000) = 12.13%. To produce exactly 6.1% on the value-weighted formula the fair value would have to be 0.061 x $1,500,000 / (0.18 - 0.061) = $768,908 - not $7,200,000. We do not have the Manager's computation or a dilution formula in the excerpts, so 6.1% is unexplained on the face of the documents; that is itself evidence of arbitrariness. VALUE OF THE OUTCOMES: 6.1% x book = $189,100; 6.1% x independent equity = $597,800; dilution redone at the correct fair value, then bought at book = 15.61% x $3,100,000 = $483,929; no dilution at all, bought at book = 18% x $3,100,000 = $558,000; no dilution at all, valued at the independent indication = $1,764,000. CAVEATS: the broker opinion was procured by the client (form, standard of value and date to be confirmed); the $3,100,000 balance sheet has not been produced and for real estate book value omits unrealized appreciation; if the $270,000 Bram paid was booked as a loan to her rather than a contribution, her percentage stays at 18% and she owes $270,000 instead; and a properly re-noticed capital call could lawfully dilute her to about 15.6%-16.3% going forward because she cannot fund $270,000 - client reports a maximum of about $60,000 (2026-10-08), and the excerpted 6.3 contains no partial-funding mechanism.
